items.q: Does SICA replace an existing academic system?
items.a: SICA can run in parallel and later become the system of record. Master data and grade history migrate in stages using an expand-and-contract scheme so there is no academic downtime.

items.q: How is one campus prevented from reading another's data?
items.a: Every business table uses a tenant_id column with default-deny Row-Level Security. The tenant context is set at the start of the transaction, so even a query that forgets to filter cannot return another tenant's rows.

items.q: Is it ready for thousands of simultaneous students?
items.a: The design target is 1,000+ concurrent users: read/write splitting, pooled database connections, per-class locking and a worker queue to finalise enrolment.

items.q: How long until it is usable?
items.a: The academic core typically goes live within weeks for one institution, depending on master data completeness and which add-on modules are activated.

items.q: Can we run it on campus servers?
items.a: Yes. The architecture supports dedicated or local cloud deployment, with releases separated from deployments behind feature flags.
